data.name: Primary Efficacy Objective
data.text: To demonstrate that 3 mg LY900018 is non-inferior to 1 mg IMG for the proportion of patients achieving treatment success from insulin-induced hypoglycemia using a non-inferiority margin of 10%

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Objective
data.text: To compare the safety and tolerability of 3 mg LY900018 with 1 mg IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Objective
data.text: To characterize the PK profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Objective
data.text: To characterize the PD profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

data.name: Exploratory Anti-glucagon Antibody Objective
data.text: Explore the formation of anti-glucagon antibodies to glucagon

data.name: Exploratory Hypoglycemia Recovery Objective
data.text: To evaluate the recovery from clinical symptoms of hypoglycemia

data.name: Primary Efficacy Endpoint
data.text: The proportion of patients achieving treatment success defined as either an increase in PG to >70 mg/dL or an increase of >20 mg/dL from nadir within 30 minutes after administration of glucagon. The nadir is defined as the minimum PG value at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration.

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Endpoint
data.text: SAE, TEAEs (including gastrointestinal, nasal, and non-nasal AEs), vital signs

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Endpoint
data.text: PK parameters include AUC, Cmax, Tmax

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Endpoint
data.text: PD parameters include BGmax and Tmax

data.name: Primary Efficacy Estimand: Non-inferiority of LY900018 vs IMG for Treatment Success
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who undergo controlled insulin-induced hypoglycemia and complete both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome. Patients with lowest PG ≥70 mg/dL at or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration, or who receive external measures to raise PG before or within 10 minutes of glucagon administration, are excluded as non-evaluable. (Full Analysis Set (all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product per treatment allocation, restricted to completers with evaluable primary outcome for primary efficacy analysis)) Summary measure: Difference in proportions (percentage of treatment successes: IMG minus LY900018) with a 2-sided 95% confidence interval derived from the 1-sample mean of paired differences in primary outcome across 2 treatment visits; non-inferiority declared if upper limit of 95% CI is less than the non-inferiority margin of 10%.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose before or within 10 minutes of glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives an external measure (e.g., IV glucose infusion) to raise PG concentration either before glucagon administration or within the first 10 minutes of glucagon administration, rendering the primary outcome non-evaluable

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose after 10 minutes post-glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion or other intervention to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia after the 10-minute post-glucagon window; data collected after such intervention may be excluded from efficacy and PD analyses

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of both treatment periods
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study before completing both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome for any reason (e.g., adverse event, withdrawal of consent, protocol deviation)

intercurrentEvents.name: Non-evaluable hypoglycemia induction: nadir PG ≥70 mg/dL
intercurrentEvents.text: The lowest PG concentration at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration is ≥70 mg/dL, indicating that adequate hypoglycemia was not achieved and the primary outcome is non-evaluable

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose by study site personnel versus 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection by study site personnel, in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product per treatment allocation, restricted to completers with evaluable primary outcome for primary efficacy analysis)
data.variableOfInterest: The proportion of patients achieving treatment success defined as either an increase in plasma glucose (PG) to ≥70 mg/dL or an increase of ≥20 mg/dL from PG nadir within 30 minutes after administration of glucagon, without receiving additional treatments to increase PG. The nadir is defined as the minimum PG value at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration.
data.summaryMeasure: Difference in proportions (percentage of treatment successes: IMG minus LY900018) with a 2-sided 95% confidence interval derived from the 1-sample mean of paired differences in primary outcome across 2 treatment visits; non-inferiority declared if upper limit of 95% CI is less than the non-inferiority margin of 10%

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: All enrolled Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who received at least one dose of investigational product, regardless of whether they completed all protocol requirements (Safety Population (all enrolled patients whether or not they completed all protocol requirements)) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics including incidence rates, frequencies, and percentages of TEAEs and SAEs by treatment group; summary statistics for vital signs changes from baseline.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation due to adverse event
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues study participation due to an adverse event following study treatment administration

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of rescue or concomitant medication for hypoglycemia or AE management
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives concomitant medications (e.g., IV glucose, antiemetics) to manage hypoglycemia or treatment-emergent adverse events during the study period

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose by study site personnel versus 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection by study site personnel
data.analysisPopulation: Safety Population (all enrolled patients whether or not they completed all protocol requirements)
data.variableOfInterest: Incidence and severity of serious adverse events (SAEs), treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) including gastrointestinal, nasal, and non-nasal adverse events, and changes in vital signs following single-dose administration
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics including incidence rates, frequencies, and percentages of TEAEs and SAEs by treatment group; summary statistics for vital signs changes from baseline

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who are randomized and receive at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable PK samples (Full Analysis Set (all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product per treatment allocation with evaluable PK data)) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, geometric mean, median, minimum, maximum) for PK parameters by treatment group; geometric mean ratios with 90% confidence intervals for AUC and Cmax comparisons between LY900018 and IMG.

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or incomplete PK blood samples
intercurrentEvents.text: One or more scheduled PK blood samples are not collected or are lost, resulting in incomplete concentration-time profiles for PK parameter estimation

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional glucose intervention affecting glucagon PK
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion or other intervention that may confound glucagon PK measurements during the sampling period

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of PK sampling
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study or is withdrawn before completion of the 4-hour post-dose PK sampling window

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose by study site personnel versus 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection by study site personnel
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product per treatment allocation with evaluable PK data)
data.variableOfInterest: Pharmacokinetic parameters including area under the concentration-time curve (AUC), maximum observed glucagon concentration (Cmax), and time to maximum concentration (Tmax) following single-dose administration, derived from serial blood samples collected immediately before and up to 4 hours post-dose
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, geometric mean, median, minimum, maximum) for PK parameters by treatment group; geometric mean ratios with 90% confidence intervals for AUC and Cmax comparisons between LY900018 and IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who are randomized and receive at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable PD (plasma glucose) measurements (Full Analysis Set (all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product per treatment allocation with evaluable PD data)) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) for PD parameters by treatment group; absolute change from baseline in plasma glucose values at various post-dose time points summarized by treatment group.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose after 10 minutes post-glucagon
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion or other intervention to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia; PG measurements taken after the time of such intervention will be excluded from PD analyses

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or incomplete PD plasma glucose samples
intercurrentEvents.text: One or more scheduled plasma glucose measurements are not collected or are lost, resulting in incomplete PD profiles

intercurrentEvents.name: Carbohydrate-rich meal administration prior to discharge
intercurrentEvents.text: All patients receive a carbohydrate-rich meal prior to discharge, which may influence late post-dose plasma glucose measurements

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose by study site personnel versus 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection by study site personnel
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product per treatment allocation with evaluable PD data)
data.variableOfInterest: Pharmacodynamic parameters including maximum observed plasma glucose concentration (BGmax) and time to maximum plasma glucose concentration (Tmax) following single-dose glucagon administration, derived from serial plasma glucose measurements collected immediately before and up to 4 hours post-dose
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) for PD parameters by treatment group; absolute change from baseline in plasma glucose values at various post-dose time points summarized by treatment group

data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who are randomized and receive at least one dose of investigational product and have evaluable antibody assessments (Full Analysis Set (all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product per treatment allocation with evaluable antibody data)) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics including frequency and percentage of patients with detectable anti-glucagon antibodies by treatment group and timepoint.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before antibody assessment
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study before the scheduled anti-glucagon antibody assessment timepoint

intercurrentEvents.name: Pre-existing anti-glucagon antibodies at baseline
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient has detectable anti-glucagon antibodies at baseline prior to study treatment administration

data.name: Exploratory Hypoglycemia Symptoms Recovery Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who are randomized and receive at least one dose of investigational product and complete the hypoglycemia symptoms questionnaire (Full Analysis Set (all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product per treatment allocation with evaluable questionnaire data)) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) for total score and subscale scores of the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale at baseline, various post-dose timepoints, and absolute change from baseline by treatment group.
